claims.claim: picks nearest selectable in each direction by position
claims.note: Automatic-mode behaviour; the Navigation Options page's Automatic row says only 'Automatic Navigation.' and the EventSystem API page does not cover automatic navigation selection.

claims.claim:
Fine for simple grids;
  breaks with irregular layouts or scroll views.
claims.note: Assessment of Automatic mode's limits; neither listed source describes where automatic navigation breaks.

claims.claim: **Horizontal / Vertical**: restrict to one axis
claims.evidence_quote: Horizontal Navigates Horizontally. Vertical Navigates Vertically. Automatic Automatic Navigation.
claims.note: The manual's mode table: the Horizontal row reads 'Navigates Horizontally.' and the Vertical row 'Navigates Vertically.', i.e. each navigates on a single axis.

claims.claim:
Horizontal would fight value change, so
  put sliders in Vertical-only lists
claims.evidence_quote: Note that the vertical sliders can't be focused-away-from using up or down keys, because they control the value of the slider.
claims.note: The manual's visualization paragraph states a slider's value axis is consumed by value control, so navigation on that axis cannot move focus away; the same is stated for horizontal sliders and left/right keys.

claims.claim: **Explicit**: set Up/Down/Left/Right targets manually
claims.evidence_quote: In this mode you can explicitly specify where the control navigates to for different arrow keys.
claims.note: The manual's Explicit row.

claims.claim: **None**: not reachable by navigation.
claims.evidence_quote: No keyboard navigation. Also ensures that it does not receive focus from clicking/tapping on it.
claims.note: The manual's None row: no keyboard navigation.

claims.claim: The **Visualize** button in the inspector draws arrows for every selectable in the scene.
claims.evidence_quote: Selecting Visualize gives you a visual representation of the navigation you have set up in the scene window.
claims.note: The manual's Visualize row; the following paragraph describes the arrows showing focus changes for the collection of controls as a group.

claims.claim:
EventSystem.current.SetSelectedGameObject(null);   // force OnSelect to fire
    EventSystem.current.SetSelectedGameObject(firstButton.gameObject);
claims.evidence_quote: Set the object as selected. Will send an OnDeselect the the old selected object and OnSelect to the new selected object.
claims.note: EventSystem.SetSelectedGameObject(GameObject) is documented on the API page (EventSystem.current returns the current EventSystem), so the null-then-select pattern deselects the old object and fires OnSelect on the newly selected one; the page's typo 'the the' is copied verbatim.

claims.claim: EventSystem "First Selected" only applies at startup.
claims.note: The API page documents the firstSelectedGameObject property ('Only one object can be selected at a time. Think: controller-selected button.') but never states when it is applied.

claims.claim: After a mouse click on empty space, selection becomes null
claims.note: Neither listed source mentions mouse clicks on empty space or the selection becoming null; the EventSystem page only defines currentSelectedGameObject.

claims.claim: if `currentSelectedGameObject == null` and a navigation input arrives
claims.note: currentSelectedGameObject is documented ('The GameObject currently considered active by the EventSystem.') but the reselect-on-navigation-input pattern appears in no listed source.

claims.claim: store it in `OnSelect` via `ISelectHandler`
claims.note: OnSelect events are named in the SetSelectedGameObject description, but ISelectHandler appears in neither listed source.

claims.claim: When closing a sub-menu, restore selection to the button that opened it.
claims.note: Practice guidance; no listed source covers restoring selection when a sub-menu closes.

claims.claim: var nav = new Navigation { mode = Navigation.Mode.Explicit };
claims.note: Neither listed source names the UnityEngine.UI Navigation struct or Navigation.Mode.Explicit; the manual documents the Explicit mode at inspector level only.

claims.note: selectOnUp is not mentioned by either listed source.

claims.claim:
nav.selectOnDown = buttons[(i + 1) % buttons.Count];
    buttons[i].navigation = nav;

claims.note: Neither listed source mentions scrolling behaviour; the uGUI ScrollRect documentation is not listed.

coverage: I chose every concrete claim in the skill - all four navigation-mode bullets including Automatic's nearest-pick behaviour and its simple-grids/scroll-views caveat, the slider value-axis advice, the Visualize button, both EventSystem selection calls with their comments, the First-Selected timing, the mouse-click selection-loss and reselect pattern with OnSelect/ISelectHandler, the sub-menu restore advice, all four code lines of the explicit-navigation block (Navigation, Navigation.Mode.Explicit, selectOnUp, selectOnDown, Selectable.navigation), the no-auto-scroll behaviour with ScrollRect.normalizedPosition and content.anchoredPosition, the InputSystemUIInputModule/StandaloneInputModule guidance, the disabled-selectables and popup behaviours, and both Verify checklist items - covering every behaviour, API name and code line since the skill has no commands, flags or numbers; I fetched both listed Unity pages with the checker's own fetcher (both 200) and set a claim confirmed only where a page states it - the Navigation Options page confirms the Horizontal, Vertical, Explicit and None modes, the slider value-axis conflict and the Visualize button, and the EventSystem API page confirms SetSelectedGameObject's OnDeselect/OnSelect semantics - while the Automatic nearest-pick behaviour, First-Selected timing, selection loss after clicks, auto-scrolling, disabled-selectable skipping, the UnityEngine.UI Navigation/Selectable C# members and InputSystemUIInputModule appear in neither page and are unverifiable, so the core code and gotcha guidance of the skill is materially uncovered.
suggested_edits: Nothing is contradicted, but most actionable claims are covered by neither listed source. A fix PR should bump version and add to sources: the uGUI API pages for UnityEngine.UI.Navigation (Navigation.Mode.Explicit, selectOnUp/selectOnDown) and UnityEngine.UI.Selectable (the navigation property and how navigation treats non-interactable or hidden selectables), UnityEngine.UI.ScrollRect (normalizedPosition, and whether selection auto-scrolls), and Input System UI documentation for InputSystemUIInputModule versus StandaloneInputModule; also cite a page stating when EventSystem.firstSelectedGameObject is applied and that clicking empty space clears the current selection. The Navigation Options manual page documents the modes at inspector level only - its Automatic row says just 'Automatic Navigation.' - so either cite a page describing automatic nearest-in-direction selection or soften that bullet to what the source states.
